title: `var` and `std`: two-pass blocks of 128, or Welford, by path
verdict: two-pass per 128-block with Chan merge (ungrouped); Welford (grouped); clamps below 0
description: Ungrouped: two-pass per block of 128 values (`mean = alg_sum(x) / n`, then `dp = alg_sum((x - mean)^2)`; `alg_sum` is a plain left fold, reassociated only on nightly Rust), blocks merged in turn by Chan's combine. The chunks of a ChunkedArray merge the same way.

Grouped, in memory: groups of indices use Welford's online variance; slice groups use the block algorithm; overlapping slices use rolling `VarState` windows. The streaming reducers insert one value at a time (Welford) or combine per chunk. So grouped and ungrouped results come from different algorithms.

A weight at most `ddof` is null: no values is null, the sample variance of one value is null, the population variance of one value is 0. `VarState::finalize` clamps a negative variance to 0 and propagates NaN; the Welford path does not clamp.

Integers and decimals become doubles first, on both engines: an integer by `as f64` (round to nearest, so 2⁶², 2⁶² + 1, 2⁶² + 2 all become 2⁶² and their variance is 0.0), a decimal by the cast to `Float64` (`dec128_to_f64`, correctly rounded; `VarStdReducer` with `needs_cast`, `Decimal`'s `var` and `agg_var`). The result is `Float64` (`Float32` for `Float32` input). `ddof` is a `u8` and the divisor `n - ddof`: Substrait's SAMPLE is `ddof=1`, POPULATION `ddof=0`.

The Python wheels build with the `nightly` feature, so `alg_add_f64` is Rust's `algebraic_add`, which lets the compiler reassociate and fuse the additions of a block's two passes: their rounding order is the compiler's, fixed per build. Welford's updates (`online_variance`, `VarState::insert_one`) and Chan's merge use plain IEEE operations.

Streaming runs `VarState` too. Ungrouped, each morsel's chunks go through the 128-value blocks and merge by Chan's formula into their pipeline's state, and the pipelines' states merge in pipeline order: block boundaries follow the morsels. Grouped, each value goes through `insert_one` (Welford) and the pipelines merge by Chan's formula. In memory, groups of indices use `online_variance` (Welford, no clamp). The two engines agree on NULL, the clamp of `VarState` and the type, and can differ in the last bits.
reference: `AggFn.var` (`varOf`, `core/Sverify/Core/Aggregate.lean`) is two-pass with native doubles in list order: the mean (`floatSum` / n), then the squared deviations from it, added from +0.0, by n or n - 1, and never below 0. A sample of one value is NULL. Only NULL and the sign are exact; engines may differ in the last bits (#54) until #85 bounds the error.

provenance.notes: `var` of one value is NULL (sample) and 0.0 (`ddof=0`); `std` of one value is NULL. Polars 2.1.0.

evidence.note: `var(ddof=1)`: the divisor is N - ddof; `var` of the Int64 column -1, 0, 1 is the Float64 1.0
`std(ddof=1)`, the same divisor; `std` of the Int64 column -1, 0, 1 is 1.0

notes: Substrait's `distribution` is `ddof`: SAMPLE is `ddof=1`, the default, and POPULATION is `ddof=0`; any other integer is allowed. The example shows an Int64 column gives a Float64 sample variance. The docs say nothing about the algorithm, about a divisor at most 0, or about decimal input.
The docs at `stable` are those of Polars 2.1.0: their [source] links point at tag py-2.1.0.

evidence.note: `VarState`: two-pass block (`alg_sum_f64`), `insert_one`, Chan's `combine`, `finalize` (null at weight ≤ ddof, clamp below 0)
`var`: values `as_()` `f64` in blocks of 128 (`CHUNK_SIZE`), merged in turn
in-memory `var`: chunks merged by `combine`
`online_variance` for groups of indices, values `to_f64`
in-memory grouped `var` of integers: `online_variance`, or the `Float64` cast for rolling slices
grouped `var`/`std` of decimals: cast to `Float64`
ungrouped `var`/`std` of decimals: cast to `Float64`
`dec128_to_f64`: the nearest `f64`
streaming: `VarStdReducer` per physical numeric type; decimals through `Float64Type` with `needs_cast`
`reduce_one` is `insert_one`, `reduce_ca` merges `moment::var` per chunk, `finish` is `finalize(ddof)`
`nightly` feature, which also turns on `simd`
`default = ["full", "nightly"]`: the wheels build with it
toolchain nightly-2026-09-01
`alg_add_f64` is `algebraic_add` under `nightly`, a plain `+` otherwise; `alg_sum_f64` folds from -0.0
ungrouped streaming reduce: each pipeline folds its morsels into a local state (`update_group`), the local states merge in pipeline order (`combine_subset`)
`VecGroupedReduction`: `update_group` calls `reduce_ca` on a morsel; `update_groups_subset` calls `reduce_one` per row
`update_groups_while_evicting` (per row `reduce_one`) and `combine_subset` (`combine`)

provenance.notes: Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). Confirms the docs-level `distribution` row: `ddof` is the divisor's offset on every path.

evidence.note: Int64 column [5]: var() null, var(ddof=0) 0.0, std() null, on both engines; Decimal(10, 2) column [5]: the same
Int64 column [2**62, 2**62 + 1, 2**62 + 2]: var() 0.0 on both engines (the exact sample variance is 1)
Decimal(10, 2) column [1.10, 2.20, 3.35]: var() 1.2658333333333334 on both engines

provenance.notes: Polars 2.1.0 (Python) from the project's environment, macOS arm64, `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=2`; each `LazyFrame` collected with `engine="in-memory"` and `engine="streaming"`.

evidence.note: `test_agg_invalid_same_engines_behavior`: `var` and `std` of one value, `Decimal`, `Float32`, `Float64`, `Int32` and others, grouped and not: the streaming engine errors exactly when the in-memory engine does, and otherwise returns the same frame
Rust `test_var`: `Int32` 5, 8, 9, 5, 0 (and with NULLs) `var(1)` is exactly 12.3
`test_decimal_agg`: `var` and `std` of a `Decimal(scale=3)` column equal those of the `Int64` column, grouped and not, within `assert_frame_equal`'s default tolerance (eager)

notes: Supports the decimal path (cast to `Float64`) and the agreement of the engines on degenerate input; the decimal test compares within a tolerance, so it does not pin the rounding. The `rounding` rows stay where they are.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory. Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), not run.

Narrowed to the in-memory engine; the streaming engine is in polars-var-std-streaming. Its ungrouped variance changes between runs (three values in five runs), which this fact did not say; grouped it agrees with the in-memory engine on the probe.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

provenance.notes: Rerun on small inputs (3,000 or 5,000 rows) in a subprocess with POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=64 and POLARS_SORT_PARTITION_THRESHOLD_BYTES=1024, which Polars reads at start-up: the same behaviour as the large inputs at the defaults (the unstable streaming sort, sums and var varying by run), so the probes stay cheap. The variables only move the thresholds; the large-input results at the defaults stand.
